The meatheads were pretty chill for the most part - a few trips to bars got a little bloody but that's about it. They generally picked fights with people their own size and most were looking to get into law enforcement after basic training or were applying to go overseas. These are the kind of guys who are an officer's wet dream and thus usually got the best treatment - and rightly so - they never suck at running/pushups or any exercises that require instant obedience.

The last bunch I'll just mix in together to include myself as well - the social outcasts. You know that person who's really nice but always talks too much or has some other social flaw? That's the rest of your platoon. All really good people, all with a trait or two that makes them hard to be around. (At 18 when I joined, I was definitely the guy who didn't shut the fuck up.) Everyone had their own thing which makes this a hard category - from the depressing to the annoying to the revolting/unhygienic.

Oh wait one last category. I've only ever met a handful of these ones, but they definitely deserve a league of their own. The patriots. The ones who have been waiting to join the army ever since they knew what it was - for the purpose of serving the country. The one in my platoon said he would, given the opportunity, fuck the queen no questions asked (Canadian Army). These guys know their military history, structure, current events, half of training before it starts and have more of their own personal military gear than army-issued kit.

So, these are the people you'll likely be working with if you decide to join the military (at an NCO level, officers are another story altogether). My main tip is to be aware of the crazies, make friends with the meatheads, learn from the patriots and help the outcasts. Training gave me some of the best and worst experiences of my life, I learned a lot about myself and the world. 10/10 would do it again.
